title: feat(driver-sql, driver-turso): schema sync indexes (created_at, id) and owner_id without a declaration
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zhuangjianguo"} -->
_Requested by **Steedos** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9Ubb?thread=cmsg_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9UbbKnsd8ZLsq9hBbRRm5JvJb2)_

Fixes #33695

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：schema sync 现在会在每张表上自动建 `(created_at, id)` 索引，也就是默认列表的排序。对象有 `owner_id` 时，再建一个 `(owner_id)` 索引，供私有 OWD 读取过滤用。Turso 远程库会建同一套隐式索引，其中也包括 #31882 引用列的索引。
- 为什么改：执行维护者裁决「两个都加」。PostgreSQL 1M 行实测，管理员默认排序页的 SQL 从 317 ms 降到 1.3 ms，HTTP p50 从 427 ms 降到 119 ms，剩下的时间主要是 count 查询。
- 风险与回滚：每张托管表多一个索引，有 owner 的表多两个，所以写入会多一份索引维护，这部分没有实测。PostgreSQL 上的已有表用 CONCURRENTLY 建索引，不锁写入。回滚就是 revert 这个 PR，已经建好的索引会留在库里，不影响正确性。SQLite 上暂时不会变快，要等 #33696（PR #33897）把 controlled-by-parent 链去掉才有收益，所以本 PR 要和 #33897 一起合，或者等它合进去之后再合。
- 先看：`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/schema-drift.ts`，关注 `IMPLICIT_SYSTEM_COLUMN_KEYS` 和 `implicitReferenceIndexesOver` 中新增的循环。然后看 `sql-driver-rotation.ts` 中启动同步的入口判断，以及 `driver-turso/src/remote-transport.ts` 的 `buildDeclaredIndexDDL`。
- 两分钟验证：`OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL=… pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-sql exec vitest run src/sql-driver-33695-system-column-indexes.test.ts`，预期 SQLite 和 live PG 两个 cell 全绿，PG 的执行计划里能看到 `idx_os33695_deal_created_at_id`。
- 需要你做的：等 PR #33897（#33696）落地后，或者和它一起，批准合并本 PR。

## What changes

The schema sync's implicit index set (`schema-drift.ts`, seeded by #31882) gains two system-column keys after the reference indexes. This follows the maintainer ruling 「两个都加」 quoted on #33695.

- `(created_at, id)`, named `idx_TABLE_created_at_id`, on every table that physically has both builtin columns.
- `(owner_id)`, named `idx_TABLE_owner_id`, on an object whose fields carry a stored, single-valued `owner_id`. An object with no `owner_id` gets no such index.

Both are non-unique and take no organization key part. A declared index whose key already STARTS WITH the whole system key serves instead: a declared `(created_at)` alone does not. A declaration of the same key converges on the same name.

Three seams carry the set:

- `sql-driver-rotation.ts` (approved surface extension): the boot sync opened `syncTableIndexes` only for objects with a unique field, an implicit reference, or declared indexes. An object with none of these would never have been given `(created_at, id)`, while the differ expected it on every boot. The sync now opens on the implicit set itself.
- `sql-driver-managed-drift.ts` (approved surface extension, one argument): `syncTableIndexes` passes `physicalColumns` to `implicitReferenceIndexes`. An adopted table without a `created_at` column is not asked to build an index it cannot have. Without this, every boot would write a false "index NOT created" line at durability level `error`.
- `driver-turso/src/remote-transport.ts`: the remote face's `buildDeclaredIndexDDL` composed only field-level unique and declared indexes. It never composed the #31882 reference indexes, while the drift differ (shared, run on both faces) expected them. It now appends `implicitReferenceIndexes(...)` against the columns it materialized. `@objectstack/driver-sql` exports `implicitReferenceIndexes` for this.

**SQLite and #33696.** This PR adds the SQLite index too, so landing waits for PR #33897 (#33696), or the two land together. That follows the card's "SQLite: land with or after the R4 card". On PostgreSQL this PR pays off alone. I did not gate SQLite by dialect. A dialect-gated set would split the one composition that the sync, the differ and both Turso faces share, and nothing measured a harm from the SQLite index: at 1M rows the chained page is unchanged (1.97 s → 1.73 s, same plan).

## Tests

- New file `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-33695-system-column-indexes.test.ts` (13 tests; the live PG cells ran) pins:
  - the expected set: both keys, no owner index without `owner_id`, the cover-by-prefix rule, name convergence, multi-valued and formula `owner_id` skipped, and no index or unbuildable report on a table with no `created_at`;
  - the SQLite boot sync: a fresh table, including an object with nothing else to index; an earlier release's table planned as `safe` `create_index`, then built, then a silent third sync; an adopted table without `created_at` with no index, no error line and no drift;
  - plans on SQLite and live PG: the default-ordered page reads `idx_os33695_deal_created_at_id` and the owner read reads `idx_os33695_deal_owner_id`;
  - PG's existing-table path: the concurrent build, then empty drift.
- New file `packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-33695-implicit-index-parity.test.ts` pins that the local and remote faces land the same names and key parts, with none on `created_by`, and that the remote plan after a remote sync proposes no index.
- Existing pins updated where the new index is now part of the set they enumerate: `sql-driver-31882-*` (`owner_id` is now indexed), `sql-driver-schema`, `sql-driver-20432-*`, `sql-driver-11321-*`, `turso-local-remote-declared-index-parity`, `turso-remote-deferred-ddl`, `turso-remote-drift-apply-limit` and `turso-remote-migration-entries`.

<details><summary>Suites on the final head (merge of origin/main), and the ablations</summary>

Under `os-verify-lock`, at head `5594216903` (after merging origin/main, then a `driver-turso...` closure build):

```
pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-sql typecheck      SQL_TC_OK
pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-turso typecheck    TURSO_TC_OK
driver-sql  Test Files 264 passed | 4 skipped (268) · Tests 5434 passed | 126 skipped (5560) · live postgres RAN
driver-turso Test Files 98 passed (98) · Tests 2543 passed | 34 skipped (2577)
VERDICT command-exit 0
```

Each ablation went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor 1 → 0, blob moved, restored from HEAD) and turned the pin red:

- A1: rotation gate closed for an object with nothing else to index. Red: "a new table gets both keys; an object with nothing else to index still gets (created_at, id)", plus the earlier-release and plan pins.
- A2: `physicalColumns` dropped from `syncTableIndexes`. Red: "an adopted table with no created_at column" (`expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times`, the durability error line).
- A3: `owner_id` presence check dropped. 5 red, including "skips a multi-valued or formula owner_id" and "a table without a created_at column … reports nothing unbuildable".
- A4: cover rule weakened to the leading column. Red: "a declared index whose key STARTS WITH the whole system key replaces it…".
- A5: Turso remote mirror filtered out. Red: both parity pins (`os33695_deal: expected { …(1) } to deeply equal { …(4) }`; remote plan `expected [ …(4) ] to deeply equal []`).

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- **Write cost NOT MEASURED.** Every managed table carries one more index, and an owned one two. The insert and update cost of maintaining them was not benched here.
- **Tenancy.** On a multi-tenant database, the default list adds `organization_id = ?`. PostgreSQL then reads `(created_at, id)` backward and filters by organization, which is fine while one tenant dominates a table. With many tenants, `(organization_id, created_at, id)` would serve better. The ruling names `(created_at, id)`, so this PR builds exactly that.
- **The owner index is chosen by selectivity.** The bench has two owners (9000 and 1000 accounts), so PostgreSQL reads `(created_at, id)` for the member's account page instead. The `owner_id` index pays off as owners multiply, and the card's own reading says so too ("grows with private-object size").
- **Rotation (ADR-0057) objects:** a throwaway probe over a rotation object showed empty drift on SQLite (the base name is a view there) and on PG (no rotation support, plain table). The probe was not committed.
- `implicitReferenceIndexes` keeps its name although it now returns the system-column keys too. Renaming it would have touched more of `sql-driver-managed-drift.ts` than the one approved argument.

## Verification

<details><summary>M0 bench (`packages/qa/dogfood/bench/sql-perf`), 1M line items, before (`63e47fee`) vs after (this branch), same box</summary>

`bench.mjs --scale 1000000 --only scoped_list_unfiltered,scoped_account_list,list_filter_sort`. The box is shared, so read the milliseconds as indicative and the plans as exact.

PostgreSQL 16 (private cluster, 1M `bench_line_item`):

| scenario | who | HTTP p50 before → after (ms) | page statement before → after (ms) |
|:--|:--|--:|--:|
| scoped_list_unfiltered | admin | 427.4 → 118.8 | 317.0 → 1.33 |
| list_filter_sort | admin | 330.8 → 141.7 | 142.4 → 3.73 |
| scoped_list_unfiltered | member | 264.9 → 83.3 | (member text not disclosed) |
| list_filter_sort | member | 252.4 → 122.3 | (member text not disclosed) |
| scoped_account_list | member | 27.2 → 23.5 | (member text not disclosed) |

`EXPLAIN ANALYZE` of the admin page as the engine emits it (chained):
- before: Parallel Seq Scan + top-N heapsort, 394.8 ms;
- after: `Index Scan Backward using idx_bench_line_item_created_at_id`, 0.253 ms.

Unchained: 119.3 → 0.025 ms. The remaining HTTP time is the page's `count(*)`, which no index here serves.

SQLite (better-sqlite3, 1M):

| scenario | who | HTTP p50 before → after (ms) |
|:--|:--|--:|
| scoped_list_unfiltered | admin | 1872.6 → 1808.1 |
| list_filter_sort | admin | 783.6 → 762.4 |
| scoped_list_unfiltered | member | 232.6 → 235.9 |
| scoped_account_list | member | 21.1 → 20.7 |

`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`:
- chained page: unchanged (`USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY`), 1968 → 1725 ms;
- the same page with the controlled-by-parent chain dropped (what #33696 does): `SCAN bench_line_item | USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY` 1578 ms → `SCAN bench_line_item USING INDEX idx_bench_line_item_created_at_id` 0.16 ms.

After schema sync, both dialects list `idx_TABLE_created_at_id` on every bench table and `sys_record_share`. `idx_TABLE_owner_id` appears on every bench object, all of which carry `owner_id`.

</details>

<details><summary>Gates</summary>

Derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, 71 families. The `--ran` reconciliation: 66 were run locally and each exited 0. `check:query-options-erasure` hit a 300 s wrapper timeout once and exited 0 on its rerun.

The PR-body gates exited 0 on this body:
- `check-changeset-no-major`
- `check-closing-keyword-parity`
- `check-adr-0087-registration`
- `check-partof-closing-keyword`

NOT MEASURED locally, left to CI's `Lint & Repo Gates` and type-check lanes: `check:dts-closure`, `check:published-files`, `check:sourcemap-no-sources-content`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:type-check-debt`. The reason: each needs a declaration build under the shared verify lock, and two 9-minute acquisitions timed out behind another seat's bundle. The typecheck of both touched packages did run against a full declaration build, as shown above.

Dependents, the test files that read indexes or drift through a driver, after a closure build at the final head, all exit 0:
- cli unit project: 2 files, 21 tests. The other named files are integration tier, CI.
- metadata-protocol `src/migrations/`: 359 tests.
- metadata overlay-index
- objectql activation-ledger
- plugin-auth stored-issuer preflight
- plugin-security permission-set guard
- service-automation connector guard
- service-messaging preference reference

`pnpm lint` is CI's. `eslint --no-inline-config` on the touched files exited 0.

</details>
